Working Towards

Tap the grade one above the grade you are working at now. If you are working at a 4, tap 5. Each tile holds the skills that move you up, with guidance, a worked example and questions that mark themselves.

How it works: score 4 out of 5 on a skill to pass it. Pass it again on a different day to master it. When every skill in a tile is mastered, the bar fills up and you are ready to move on. Your progress is saved on this phone or computer only.

Your tier

Both papers are tiered. You will sit either Foundation (grades 1 to 5) or Higher (grades 4 to 9). Check with your teacher which tier you are doing.

Equipment

A pen, pencil, ruler, protractor, compasses, rubber, and a calculator for Paper 2 only.

How to prepare

  • Read through the tasks and questions you answered in lessons in your exercise book.
  • Missed a lesson? Catch up by asking your teacher, or a classmate, what you missed.
  • Practise exam-style questions on the Student Essentials page, and with the practice sets below.

To get the very top marks

  • Show your working clearly. Method marks are given even when the final answer is wrong.
  • Check your answers and calculations at the end of the exam.
  • Practise with the calculator you will take into Paper 2, so you know where every button is.

Know your three papers

Three papers, one qualification. Each is 1 hour 30, worth 80 marks, and counts exactly a third. Any topic can appear on any paper: you cannot revise "by paper", only by topic.

Paper 1 · 8300/1

Non-calculator

1h 30m · 80 marks · 33⅓% · Fri 14 May 2027 (am)
  • No calculator: arithmetic is being tested on purpose
  • Fractions often beat decimals here: ⅓ is exact, 0.333… is not
  • Know your times tables, squares to 152, cubes of 1–5 and 10
  • Exact trig values (sin 30° = 12 etc.) love this paper
Golden rule: show working for every mark. A wrong answer with correct method still earns method marks: a bare wrong answer earns nothing.
Paper 2 · 8300/2

Calculator

1h 30m · 80 marks · 33⅓% · Thu 27 May 2027 (am)
  • Calculator allowed, and expected. Bring a scientific one you know
  • Write down the full calculator display before rounding
  • Use the fraction button, S⇔D, and ANS to avoid re-typing
  • Check DEGREE mode before any trigonometry
Examiner intel: "You must show your working" means it: a correct answer alone can score zero on those questions.
Paper 3 · 8300/3

Calculator

1h 30m · 80 marks · 33⅓% · Mon 14 Jun 2027 (am)
  • Same rules as Paper 2, and the last exam of the series
  • Sat over two weeks after Paper 1: keep revising between papers
  • Topics that didn't appear on Papers 1–2 very often turn up here
  • After each paper, list what hasn't come up yet, then revise that
Strategy: the gap between papers is revision time most students waste. Papers 1 and 2 tell you exactly what Paper 3 is likely to ask.

Foundation or Higher: how the tiers work

Foundation (grades 1–5)Higher (grades 4–9)
Grades available1 2 3 4 54 5 6 7 8 9
The overlapGrades 4 and 5 can be earned on either tier, but a Higher student performing below grade 4 level risks a U. All three papers must be the same tier.
What's differentBasic + additional foundation content only. More marks for standard techniques.Everything Foundation covers, plus Higher-only content. More reasoning and problem-solving marks.

Where the marks live: topic weightings

Set by Ofqual, identical for every exam board. This is your revision-time budget: Higher students, algebra is nearly a third of your exam. Foundation students, number and ratio are half of yours.

Topic areaFoundationHigherWhat that means
Number25%15%Foundation's biggest earner. FDP, calculation, standard form.
Algebra20%30%Higher's biggest earner by a distance. No algebra, no grade 7+.
Ratio, proportion & rates of change25%20%Huge on both tiers: percentages, proportion, compound measures.
Geometry & measures15%20%Angles, area/volume, Pythagoras & trig, circle theorems (H).
Probability & Statistics15%15%The most predictable questions on the paper. Bank these marks.

The three assessment objectives: what a question is really testing

AOWeighting F / HWhat it testsHow to spot it
AO150% / 40%Use and apply standard techniques: recall, notation, routine procedures."Work out", "Solve", "Simplify", "Factorise". Do the method, show the steps.
AO225% / 30%Reason, interpret and communicate mathematically."Show that", "Prove", "Give a reason", "Explain why". Every line must follow logically, and end with a conclusion.
AO325% / 30%Solve problems: translate a situation into maths, choose the method yourself.Wordy, real-life setups with no named method. Your first job is deciding what maths this is.

Command words: the question tells you the answer's shape

CommandIt means
Write down / StateNo working needed: it's a 1-mark recall or read-off. Don't waste time.
Work out / CalculateWorking IS needed. "Calculate" hints the calculator is useful (Papers 2–3).
EstimateRound every value to 1 significant figure first, then calculate. Do NOT work exactly and round at the end, that scores zero.
Show thatThe answer is given: the marks are ALL in the working. Reach the printed result with clear, complete steps.
ProveFormal reasoning: algebra set up in general terms (2n, 2n+1…), every step justified, and a closing statement.
HenceYou MUST use the previous part. "Hence or otherwise": "hence" is nearly always faster.
Simplify fully / Factorise fully"Fully" is a warning: one more step exists. 2(2x+4) is not fully factorised; 4(x+2) is.
Give a reasonQuote the geometric fact by its full name: "alternate angles are equal", not "Z angles".
You must show your workingAn unsupported answer, even a correct one, can score zero on this question.

How your script is actually marked

AQA examiners award marks by type. Once you know the codes, "show your working" stops being teacher advice and becomes a scoring strategy.

MarkNameEarned by
M1Method markA correct method, even with wrong numbers carried in. This is why working = marks.
A1Accuracy markThe correct answer following a correct method. Usually can't be earned without the M mark.
B1Independent markA correct fact or value on its own: no method required.
ftFollow-throughMarks for correctly using your own earlier (wrong) answer. One slip doesn't sink the question.
The cheapest marks in GCSE maths: writing one line of method on a question you can't finish. Examiners award M1 for a correct first step constantly: blank space is the only guaranteed zero.

The formulae sheet: given vs memorise

You WILL get a formulae sheet in your exam, but it covers only a fraction of what you need, and AQA is banned from asking questions you can answer just by copying from it. Full breakdown in the Formulae tab.

The Federation route through the course

These are the actual units, in the actual order, from the Harris KS4 scheme of work, so this app always matches what your teacher is teaching. Tap a unit to see what you must be able to do and the trap examiners report every year. Switch tier above.

Given on your formulae sheet

A clean copy comes with every paper (confirmed for 2027 and beyond). Practise finding and using these fast: questions will never be pure copy-outs.

BOTH TIERS  Circumference C = πd = 2πr · Area of a circle A = πr2
BOTH TIERS  Pythagoras a2 + b2 = c2 · Trig ratios sin θ = opphyp cos θ = adjhyp tan θ = oppadj
BOTH TIERS  Area of a trapezium 12(a + b)h · Volume of a prism area of cross-section × length
BOTH TIERS  Compound interest P(1 + r100)n · Relative frequency ≈ probability over n trials
HIGHER ONLY  Quadratic formula x = −b ± √b2 − 4ac2a
HIGHER ONLY  Sine rule asin A = bsin B · Cosine rule a2 = b2 + c2 − 2bc cos A · Area 12ab sin C
HIGHER ONLY  Probability P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) · P(A and B) = P(A given B) × P(B)

Given inside the question, when needed

BOTH TIERS  Volume of a sphere 43πr3 · Volume of a cone 13πr2h · Volume of a pyramid 13 × base area × h
BOTH TIERS  Surface area of a sphere 4πr2 · Curved surface of a cone πrl
These appear printed in the question itself, but you must know how to rearrange and combine them.

NOT given: memorise cold

This list is longer than the sheet. These score marks only if they're in your head on the day.

BOTH  Area: triangle 12bh · parallelogram b×h · Speed S = DT · Density D = MV · Pressure P = FA
BOTH  Straight line y = mx + c · Gradient ΔyΔx · Percentage multipliers (+8% → ×1.08, −8% → ×0.92)
BOTH  Index laws am×an=am+n aman = am−n (am)n=amn a0=1 · Angle facts & polygon rules (exterior angles sum to 360°)
BOTH  Exact trig values: sin 30° = 12 cos 60° = 12 sin 45° = cos 45° = √22 tan 45° = 1 sin 60° = cos 30° = √32 tan 30° = √33 tan 60° = √3: yes, Foundation too.
HIGHER  Circle theorems (all seven, with exact wording) · a−n = 1an · amn = (n√a)m · Completing the square · Direct/inverse proportion forms y = kx, y = kx, y = kx2
Sheet discipline: in practice papers, use a printed copy of the real AQA sheet, nothing more. Training with a full formula booklet teaches you to rely on formulae that won't be there.
